items.capacity: Managing Director, International Affairs (London-based; government relations outside North America)
items.fact: The Guardian (2 Sept 2026, reprinted by Freevacy) reports that Clifford has joined Anthropic as Managing Director, International Affairs, covering government relations outside the US across the UK, Europe, India and Asia-Pacific. Times Higher Education (7 Sept 2026) reports he stepped down as founding chair of ARIA that day, citing the Anthropic role; no Anthropic press release was found.
items.quote: has joined US startup Anthropic as managing director of international affairs
items.missing: Exact start date (2026-09 is the reported announcement month; no start date is given in the sources read); an Anthropic press release or statement (none found); any ACOBA or successor advice on this move (none found; gov.uk says ACOBA ceased operating on 13 Oct 2025, with ministers' applications going to the Independent Adviser on Ministerial Standards and Crown servants' to the Civil Service Commission).
items.notes: Earlier roles: founding chair of ARIA since its 2022 inception (THE, 7 Sept 2026); previously Keir Starmer's AI opportunities adviser before stepping down (Guardian reprint; dates not read). Anthropic's reported position: Clifford makes no procurement or spending decisions at ARIA and will recuse himself from decisions affecting Anthropic (Guardian reprint). Date conflict unresolved: THE reports a 7 Sept 2026 resignation, while a search headline (aiweekly, not read) says he would leave ARIA by 6 Nov 2026. Select committee chair Chi Onwurah said questions remain (THE).

items.capacity: Senior Advisor, paid appointment (gov.uk ACOBA letter title: Senior Advisor, Anthropic PBC)
items.fact: The ACOBA advice letter on gov.uk (page updated 9 Oct 2025) approved a paid Anthropic PBC appointment for the former Prime Minister, subject to conditions. The conditions bar use of privileged information and, for two years from his last day in ministerial office, personal involvement in lobbying the UK government or its arm's-length bodies for Anthropic; press reports dated the announcement to October 2025.
items.quote: The advice imposes a number of conditions to mitigate the potential risks
items.missing: Actual start date and whether the role is still current (no source read gives a start date); the separate press-reported LinkedIn post of 9 Oct 2025 was not read directly.
items.notes: Former Prime Minister and MP. The letter records his confirmation that the role will not include advising on specific UK policy matters and is internally oriented, with no lobbying. A separate ACOBA letter on the same gov.uk publication covers his Microsoft senior adviser role. This item also answers brief item 5 for Sunak.

items.capacity: External Affairs, paid full-time role (gov.uk ACOBA letter title: External Affairs, Anthropic PBC)
items.fact: page read: ACOBA advice letter (published 24 June 2025) on a paid, full-time External Affairs role at Anthropic PBC for Lord Booth-Smith, formerly Chief of Staff at No.10 Downing Street and described in the letter as a Special Adviser. The letter says his work excludes any lobbying of the UK government, which former senior Crown servants are barred from for two years, and that Anthropic confirmed this in writing.
items.missing: Start date (not stated; the letter describes him as seeking to take up the role); date he left No.10; whether he is still in the role. One aggregator snippet says he joined in 2026, which conflicts with the 2025 letter and was not verified.
items.notes: The letter cites the February 2025 DSIT Memorandum of Understanding with Anthropic as background (an institutional item, not a personnel move). The letter says Anthropic is building a UK presence that includes work across the UK government. He is a member of the House of Lords, so the letter also reminds him of the Lords code on paid lobbying.

items.capacity: External Affairs (London), Policy Division; previously Deputy Director, AI International Policy, DSIT
items.fact: page read: the DSIT business-appointment record (January to March 2025 entries) lists Daisy McGregor, Deputy Director, AI International Policy, as leaving the Civil Service on 28 Feb 2025 and joining Anthropic in External Affairs (London), Policy Division from 18 Mar 2025. The Department approved the appointment subject to conditions, including no commercial discussions involving Anthropic while in Crown service and, from her last day, no personal involvement in lobbying the UK government for Anthropic on policies that would benefit it.
items.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (gov.uk business-appointment transparency record)
items.missing: Current title after March 2025 (no public profile found in 14 searches); the record's publication date; the full wording of the lobbying condition and its duration (not fully read).
items.notes: This is the DSIT record for a former civil servant moving into Anthropic's London policy team, so it bears on brief items 2 and 3. Her earlier DSIT role is stated in the same record.

items.capacity: Member of Technical Staff (previously DSIT Head of AI Engineering)
items.fact: page read: the DSIT business-appointment record lists James Lowe, Head of AI Engineering, as leaving the Civil Service on 1 Dec 2025 and joining Anthropic as Member of Technical Staff from 2 Dec 2025. The Department's conditions bar him, for the rest of his Crown service, from commercial discussions that could later involve Anthropic.
items.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (gov.uk business-appointment transparency record)
items.missing: Any public profile confirming the role; whether he has any policy function (the record gives only a technical title).
items.notes: Technical role, not policy. A search summary had named David Knott as the DSIT official who joined Anthropic; the same DSIT record shows Knott (Government Chief Technology Officer) leaving on 31 Dec 2025 for self-employed consultancy and board roles, with no Anthropic link. That claim is rejected.

items.capacity: Chief Global Affairs Officer (first holder); manages relations with policymakers and governments where Anthropic is expanding
items.fact: page read: Business Today (5 Aug 2026, citing Reuters) reports that Anthropic named Cuéllar its first chief global affairs officer, with responsibility for its standing with policymakers, regulators and governments and for engagement in countries where it is expanding. This is an international policy lead, not a UK public-body move.
items.quote: Cuéllar reportedly brings government experience and expertise in AI policy
items.missing: Earlier public roles (the page read gives only 'government experience' and no titles or dates); a primary Anthropic announcement; start date (only the announcement date is given).
items.notes: Earlier roles not in the pages read. A search summary (not verified on a page) says the UK international role reports into the group Cuéllar leads.

items.capacity: Head of UK, Ireland and Northern Europe (Anthropic's GOV.UK partnership quote); Erevena post gives Head of UK&I and Northern Europe
items.fact: page read: Anthropic's own GOV.UK partnership announcement (published 27 Jan 2026) quotes Pip White as Head of UK, Ireland and Northern Europe. An Erevena post (20 Jan 2026) announces the appointment of three EMEA regional leaders, including White, to Head of UK&I and Northern Europe; that is a country-leadership title rather than a policy title.
items.quote: commented Pip White, Head of UK, Ireland and Northern Europe
items.missing: Start date (2026-01 is the Erevena announcement month and is not confirmed by Anthropic); earlier public role (not found); whether the role has a policy remit.
items.notes: Erevena post (erevena.com, 20 Jan 2026) is the appointment announcement. No earlier public role was found in the searches.

items.capacity: UK Head of Policy, referred to in a London Policy Advisor, UK job listing; holder not named
items.fact: page not read: this rests on search snippets of a London Policy Advisor, UK job listing that says the role works in coordination with a UK Head of Policy. No named holder was found in 14 searches.
items.quote: in coordination with the UK Head of Policy
items.missing: Name, dates and public record of the UK Head of Policy; the job listing itself was not read.
items.notes: One listing (per search summary) shows an application window that closed 7 Jan 2026. The named UK leader found is Pip White (T2.7).

items.fact: page not read for AISI, ARIA or No 10 personnel announcements: no search result named an Anthropic employee who joined AISI, ARIA, DSIT or No 10. The DSIT transparency records read list Anthropic only for the Lowe and McGregor moves into Anthropic.
